name: Stitchway
summary: A checkout stepper where a needle sews each finished step's button on and stitches the seam ahead
about: A four-step order form for a tailored kurta, with the steps drawn as sewing buttons on a tailor's chalk line. Finish a step and the needle lifts, crosses the button with thread, then runs along the seam stitch by stitch to the next one while lint flies off; a wrong field makes it prick the button. Fabric, fit, delivery and payment all really work, with a kurta drawing that follows your measurements, PKR totals and a swing tag when the order is placed.
how: Pick a fabric and colour, then press Next; the needle sews that step's button on.
Tap a size to fill the measurements or type your own in inches; the kurta drawing follows.
Fill name, an 11 digit mobile starting with 03 and a city; tap a sewn button or Back to go back.
Place the order to tie off the thread; a demo plays until you click, tap or press a key.
